solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Leading actor isn’t shifting sets about (6,2)

indicators.note: letters that shift move around, so ISNT is rearranged

blocks.note: the star is the lead in a show
ISNT rearranged

annotation.surface: A lead actor fussing because the stage sets won't move.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leading actor' looks like the definition, and a leading actor does star in things, but it only supplies STAR; the definition is 'sets about', to begin.
annotation.definitionFit: To start in on something, or starts in, is to set about it, to begin.

entries.clue: View team at the Oval taking five for one run (6)

indicators.note: the team takes on a new letter
one thing in place of another, so V replaces R

blocks.note: Surrey County Cricket Club plays at the Oval, a London cricket ground
V is five in Roman numerals
R = run in cricket scoring; one of SURREY's two Rs goes

annotation.surface: Watching a cricket team at the Oval as a bowler takes five wickets for one run.
annotation.walkthrough: Only one of SURREY's two Rs is replaced, which is why the clue says 'one run'. The cricket picture of five wickets for one run is a false scorecard.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to survey is to look over a whole scene, a more formal word for view.

entries.clue: Quinquireme of Nineveh, say, bringing back some ivory so gracefully (6)

indicators.note: back reads the letters right to left
only some of the letters are used, so the answer is inside the phrase

blocks.note: ivor(Y SO GRA)cefully, then read backwards

annotation.surface: A line from Masefield's poem Cargoes, where a quinquireme of Nineveh rows home with ivory.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition quotes John Masefield's poem Cargoes, which opens with the quinquireme of Nineveh carrying ivory; 'say' marks it as one example of a grand merchant ship.
annotation.definitionFit: An argosy is a large merchant ship, and the quinquireme laden with treasure in Cargoes is a fine example.

entries.clue: Regularly flooded expanse at all fit for development around delta? (5,4)

indicators.note: fit for development means ready to be reshaped, so the letters are rearranged
the rearranged letters go round the D

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters
D is delta in the phonetic alphabet, taken inside

annotation.surface: Asking whether marshy land by a river delta is fit to be built on.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a planning question about land by a river delta; the delta is only the letter D, and the tidal flat is flooded by the tide twice a day, hence 'Regularly'.
annotation.definitionFit: A tidal flat is a stretch of mud or sand covered at high tide and exposed at low tide.

entries.clue: Brief noisy disturbance below in street (12)

annotation.definitionNote: Brief is a singular noun here; instructions is its plural equivalent, as a lawyer's brief is a set of instructions.

indicators.note: in a down clue, below puts RUCTIONS under IN ST

blocks.note: used as it stands
ST is the address abbreviation for street
ructions are noisy rows or uproar

annotation.surface: A short scuffle breaking out down in the street.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brief' looks like an adjective, short, describing the disturbance; it is the noun, the brief given to a barrister.
annotation.definitionFit: A brief is a set of instructions, especially those given to a barrister on a case.

entries.clue: West London area to deposit money from East? (6)

indicators.note: in an across clue, reading from the east end means right to left

blocks.note: to put something down is to deposit it
the yen is Japan's currency, money from the East

annotation.surface: A West London bank taking a deposit of money from the Far East.
annotation.walkthrough: 'from East' works twice: the yen is Eastern money, and it is read from the east, backwards. Putney is a district on the Thames in south-west London.
annotation.definitionFit: Putney is a district of south-west London on the Thames, where the Boat Race starts.

entries.clue: Greek character switched on light without guidance (5)

indicators.note: the two letters swap round, NU to UN
in a down clue, UN sits on top of LED

blocks.note: nu is the Greek letter N
an LED, light-emitting diode, is a light

annotation.surface: A Greek letter lit up by a switched-on light, as if on a sign.
annotation.walkthrough: 'switched on light' reads as one phrase about a lamp; 'switched' acts on NU and 'on' joins it to LED.
annotation.definitionFit: Unled means not led, having no one to guide it.

entries.clue: Maiden invigorating after man of gravity (8)

annotation.definitionNote: An adjectival phrase: after a person means in their manner or style.

blocks.note: a maiden voyage or speech is a new, first one
a tonic is invigorating, and as an adjective tonic means invigorating

annotation.surface: A young woman bracing after a solemn man.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Maiden' wants to be M or a girl; it is used adjectivally, new. The man of gravity is Isaac Newton, who described gravitation, not a solemn man.
annotation.definitionFit: Newtonic means relating to or in the manner of Newton, so 'after' him in the sense of following his style.

entries.clue: Drinks that are long absent from US domestic market? (4,4)

indicators.note: what is absent is missing, so OF drops out

blocks.note: a yard of ale is a long glass of beer about a yard tall
of = from, as in 'a man of Kent'; removed

annotation.surface: Long drinks that you can't buy in American shops.
annotation.walkthrough: A yard of ale is a British pub novelty, a metre-long glass drunk in one go. The question mark admits that a yard sale is 'domestic' only in the sense of being held at home.
annotation.definitionFit: A yard sale is the American name for selling off household goods in your front yard, a domestic market in two senses.

entries.clue: Doctor that is most unlikely to bow (8)

blocks.note: to doctor results is to rig them
id est, Latin for 'that is', abbreviated i.e.

annotation.surface: A doctor who refuses ever to bow to anyone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reads as a noun, a physician; it is the verb, to falsify. 'that is' is written out in full Latin, ID EST.
annotation.definitionFit: The most rigid thing is the stiffest, least able to bend or bow.

entries.clue: Phone left in lady’s chamber (6)

indicators.note: 'in' places one thing inside another, so the lady's chamber holds the L

blocks.note: a bower is a lady's private room in old poetry
L = left

annotation.surface: A telephone left behind in a lady's private chamber.
annotation.walkthrough: The blower is old British slang for the telephone.
annotation.definitionFit: Blower is British slang for the telephone, as in 'get on the blower'.

entries.clue: Entertaining music’s tempo not affected with dodgy bar right before (12)

indicators.note: affected means altered, so NOT is rearranged
DIVE R goes before the rest

blocks.note: a dive is a seedy bar
R = right
time, as in the speed of a piece of music
NOT rearranged

annotation.surface: Complaining that a piece's tempo was unaffected even with a shaky bar before it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'not affected' reads as unchanged, but 'affected' is the signal to rearrange the word before it. The 's is 'has', joining definition to wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A divertimento is a light piece of instrumental music written to entertain, often for social occasions.

entries.clue: Moderate and Liberal stand in studio (5)

blocks.note: to ease is to moderate or lessen
L = Liberal

annotation.surface: A moderate and a Liberal politician standing for election in a TV studio.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is political, a centrist and a Liberal; 'stand' is a support, not a candidacy.
annotation.definitionFit: An easel is the stand an artist props a canvas on in the studio.

entries.clue: Shower parts I put in leaked by sinks (9)

indicators.note: to put something in is to insert it, so I goes inside RAN
by means next to, so DROPS follows

blocks.note: a leaking tap ran
used as it stands
to sink is to drop

annotation.surface: A plumber explaining that the shower parts they fitted leaked into the sinks.
annotation.walkthrough: The bathroom picture, a shower, parts, sinks, a leak, hides a weather shower.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by parts: a shower of rain is made of many drops, so these are its parts, not the plumbing the surface suggests.

entries.clue: College pinks trashed bars sounding well hammered (12)

indicators.note: something trashed is wrecked, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters

annotation.surface: Students in college colours wrecking pubs and ending up drunk.
annotation.walkthrough: 'trashed', 'bars' and 'hammered' paint a drunken student night; 'hammered' is struck with hammers, and 'bars' are metal bars.
annotation.definitionFit: A glockenspiel is a set of tuned metal bars struck with small hammers, sounding well when hammered.

entries.clue: Use abrasive cleaning spray on son with bother (9)

blocks.note: S = son
and = with, together
'Blast!' and 'Bother!' are both mild curses

annotation.surface: Instructions to spray a cleaning product on your son, with some fuss.
annotation.walkthrough: 'bother' is the exclamation, not trouble: 'Bother!' and 'Blast!' say the same thing.
annotation.definitionFit: To sandblast a surface is to clean it with a high-pressure spray of sand, an abrasive.

entries.clue: Members standing by one who is lying? (8)

annotation.definition: Members standing by one who is lying?

blocks.note: on the surface, loyal party members; really upright limbs standing beside something
on the surface a liar; really someone lying down, asleep

annotation.surface: Party members loyally backing a colleague caught out telling lies.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Members standing by' suggests loyal colleagues and 'lying' a liar; the lying is lying down in bed, and the members are its upright limbs.
annotation.definitionFit: Bedposts are the upright members at a bed's corners, standing by its sleeper.

entries.clue: Foolish new couple spurning wife’s wealth (8)

indicators.note: foolish suggests silly behaviour, so the letters are jumbled
spurning something rejects it, so the W is left out

blocks.note: used as it stands; its W is the wife that gets spurned
used as it stands
W = wife, removed

annotation.surface: A silly newlywed pair turning their noses up at the wife's money.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the wordplay to 'wealth'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: lavish, showy wealth, the kind a fortune-hunting couple might covet.

entries.clue: Deporting, for instance, stopped by unknown power courts preserve (12)

indicators.note: EG is plugged by the rest, which goes inside it

blocks.note: e.g., for example
x is the algebraic unknown
P = power in physics
atria are open inner courts, plural of atrium
to tin food is to preserve it

annotation.surface: An example of deportation blocked by an unknown power in the courts.
annotation.walkthrough: The legal surface of deportation and courts makes 'courts' look like law courts; they are atria, courtyards.
annotation.definitionFit: To expatriate someone is to banish them from their country, which is deporting.

entries.clue: Director’s business upset alpha males in charge (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the letters upside down, bottom to top

blocks.note: A is alpha, the phonetic alphabet's first letter
men are males
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

annotation.surface: A company director upset that alpha males are running things.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Director' reads as a company boss; it is a film director, and 'alpha males in charge' is three separate pieces, not one phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: Cinema is the film industry, the business a film director works in.

entries.clue: Part of France that’s almost too wonderful (6)

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so the last letter of ALSO goes

blocks.note: ALSO, too, without its last letter
ace = excellent, wonderful

annotation.surface: A region of France that is nearly too lovely.
annotation.walkthrough: 'too' means also, not excessively.
annotation.definitionFit: Alsace is a region in north-eastern France, on the Rhine.

entries.clue: With nothing to eat, glum pony chewed knotweed (9)

indicators.note: the anagram eats the O, taking it inside
chewed food is mashed up, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: O looks like zero, nothing
anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: A sad hungry pony reduced to chewing weeds.
annotation.walkthrough: The ordered assembly puts the O inside the rearranged GLUMPONY: POLYG(O)NUM.
annotation.definitionFit: Polygonum is the botanical genus of knotweeds.

entries.clue: Fool from Sydney in hospital after big party (5)

indicators.note: 'after' means following in sequence, so H is written following GALA

blocks.note: a gala is a big festive occasion
H = hospital, as on road signs

annotation.surface: An Australian idiot ends up in hospital after a big party.
annotation.walkthrough: A galah is an Australian cockatoo, and Australian slang for a fool.
annotation.definitionFit: In Australian slang a galah, after the noisy pink cockatoo, is a fool.

entries.clue: Fish on front of barbecue turning black? (5)

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter
turning into something else, so G becomes B

blocks.note: a barbecue is a grill
B = black on pencils; it replaces the G

annotation.surface: Fish left on the barbecue until it turns black.
annotation.walkthrough: 'turning black' pictures burnt fish; it is the first letter of GRILL turning into B.
annotation.definitionFit: Brill is a European flatfish related to the turbot.

entries.clue: Latterly wandering Serpentine’s banks and Long Water (6)

indicators.note: the banks of a lake are its edges, so only the first and last letters count

blocks.note: first and last letters of SERPENTINE
the Nile, the world's longest river

annotation.surface: Strolling round the Serpentine and the Long Water, the two linked lakes of Hyde Park and Kensington Gardens in London.
annotation.walkthrough: The Long Water really is part of the Serpentine lake in London, which is why 'Long Water' looks like a place name; here it is the long river NILE. 'Wandering' is mental, not walking.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone senile has a mind that wanders, in later life, hence 'latterly'.

entries.clue: Old Americans remain married in retirement out of the public eye (2,6)

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so ARE M reads backwards

blocks.note: the Inca were a people of ancient Peru
to be or remain, as in 'there are three left'
M = married

annotation.surface: An elderly American couple staying married after retiring to a quiet life.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old Americans' reads as retired pensioners; they are the Inca. In camera is a legal term for a hearing held in private.
annotation.definitionFit: In camera, Latin 'in the chamber', means in private, away from the public, as for a closed court hearing.

entries.clue: Boil what little supporters brought over (6)

indicators.note: turned over, so EH TEES reads backwards

blocks.note: 'Eh?' and 'What?' both ask someone to repeat
a golf tee is a small peg supporting the ball

annotation.surface: Asking what a group of young fans brought along to the match.
annotation.walkthrough: 'little supporters' reads as young fans; they are golf tees.
annotation.definitionFit: To seethe is to boil or churn, and in older English it simply meant to boil.

entries.clue: Row eight in this? (4,4)

blocks.note: on the surface a numbered row of seats; really the verb, to row as one of a crew of eight
the event itself, an annual contest between two eights

annotation.surface: Looks like a seating instruction: row eight in this theatre.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Row' pretends to be a line of seats; it is the verb, to row. The Boat Race is the annual Oxford v Cambridge rowing race on the Thames, starting at Putney.
annotation.definitionFit: The Boat Race is contested by two eight-oared crews, so you row as one of eight in it.
